title: What's next for Wings? After Paige Bueckers' playoff debut, Dallas must shore up supporting cast - CBS Sports
description: For the majority of last Friday night's winner-take-all Game 3 between the Dallas Wings and Golden State Valkyries, it seemed that the W
body:
For the majority of last Friday night's winner-take-all Game 3 between the Dallas Wings and Golden State Valkyries, it seemed that the Wings were going to pull off a remarkable upset and advance to the semifinals for the first time since 2023. Instead, their 16-point lead kept slowly melting away until, with just over a minute left, it disappeared for good when Gabby Williams hit a go-ahead jumper. At the podium, shortly after a heartbreaking end to her sophomore campaign and postseason debut, Paige Bueckers was asked what stood out about this team and what they accomplished. "I think just our selfless nature and how much we enjoyed coming to work," Bueckers said, before pausing and burying her head in her towel, unable to hold back tears. After another All-WNBA-caliber season, Bueckers scored just 27 points on 27 shots in the final two games of the series while battling the Valkyries' relentless defense and a patellar tendinitis flare-up in her right knee that had limited her since the World Cup. Despite how things ended, the Wings' 2026 campaign should be seen as a success, both inside and outside the locker room. 
After winning 19 combined games in 2024 and 2025, the Wings made wholesale changes last offseason. They replaced Chris Koclanes with Jose Fernandez, signed Jessica Shepard and Alanna Smith in free agency and drafted Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 overall pick. In addition, they re-signed franchise stalwart Arike Ogunbowale. Back in the spring, there were real questions about how the new-look group was going to fare, especially given the organization's poor track record. How would Fernandez translate to the professional game after more than two decades at South Florida? Would Shepard and Smith be enough to shore up the frontcourt? Was Fudd, who is in a relationship with Bueckers, the right choice at No. 1? And did it make sense to bring Ogunbowale back into a crowded backcourt after the worst season of her career? Fernandez going on a lengthy postgame rant calling his players selfish after a 1-2 start didn't ease any of the concerns. But the Wings responded to Fernandez's challenge and won six of their next seven games, and by late July were sitting in fourth place thanks in large part to a breakout season from Shepard, who went on to win Most Improved Player and proved to be a far more impactful signing than Smith. 
The Wings stumbled on either side of the All-Star break, however, and in late August Fudd was ruled out for the season due to a knee injury that required surgery. By that point, the Wings were stuck in eighth place and had some work to do to fend off the expansion Portland Fire for the final playoff spot. While everyone expected they would, there was little hope for the rest of the season without Fudd. Even after they won seven of their final eight games to finish 27-17 -- a record-setting 17-win improvement on last season -- and earn the No. 7 seed, no one expected their first playoff appearance since 2023 to last long. A 24-point loss to the Valkyries in Game 1 only confirmed those thoughts. Ogunbowale would not let her team go down without a fight, however. She set the WNBA record for points in a playoff game with a heroic 45-point outing in Game 2, which included an absurd 3-pointer from deep in the corner to force overtime, and added another 30 points in Game 3 to nearly complete the upset. If she hadn't tweaked her groin in the fourth quarter of that game, which forced her to briefly go to the locker room, the Wings may still be playing right now. 
As it is, they're sitting at home, but with hope for the future. "I knew we were on the right trajectory when we got Paige," Ogunbowale said last Friday while an emotional Bueckers sat beside her. "Generational player. She willed us throughout the whole season, should be First Team All-WNBA. If not, I feel like that shit's rigged, because she's done everything for this team. I said it in signing back, I saw the vision."Season at a glanceRecord: 27-17 (No. 7 seed)Offensive rating: 111.3 (5th)Defensive rating: 106.4 (6th)Net rating: plus-6.8 (5th)Biggest strengthJump shootingNo team took more jumpers than the Wings this season, who fired 43.7 per game and 1,922 in total. They were a league-best 46.5% on 2-point jumpers and shot 34.8% from 3-point range, which ranked fifth in the league. All told, their 1.001 points per possession on jumpers ranked fifth. On an individual level, Paige Bueckers took 530 jumpers -- 69 more than any other player -- and among the 88 players who took at least 100 jumpers, no one shot better than her 47.2%. Arike Ogunbowale (367) and Azzi Fudd (268) ranked ninth and 21st, respectively, in jump shot attempts, and Fudd would have been even higher if not for a season-ending knee injury. When those jumpers were going in, the Wings were really tough to beat. 
Biggest weaknessPerformances against other playoff teamsThe Wings went 27-17 by beating up on lottery opponents. They were a remarkable 20-2 against the seven lottery teams, and both defeats -- against the Portland Fire and Phoenix Mercury -- were by a single point. By contrast, they were 7-15 against the seven other playoff teams, which obviously was not good enough and cost them a higher seed in the playoffs. Key free agentsAwak Kuier (restricted)Maddy Siegrist (restricted)Alysha Clark (unrestricted)Biggest question: How do they build out the supporting cast? The Wings don't have many free agents, but they still face an interesting offseason, in which they'll have to figure out which players they view as long-term fits alongside Bueckers and Fudd, and how they want to build out their supporting cast. As great as it was to win 17 more games this season, make the playoffs for the first time since 2023 and push the Valkyries to the limit, this team is still a few moves away from becoming a true contender. First and foremost, the Wings will have to address Kuier's restricted free agency. The former No. 2 overall pick returned to the WNBA this season after sitting out in 2024 and 2025, and though she didn't play much early on, became a key piece down the stretch. She is by far the best interior defender on the team, and after the All-Star break, led the league in blocks per game (2.6). Additionally, she shot 39% from 3-point range, and though her shot can be streaky, her ability to space the floor on the offensive end makes her a unique talent. Kuier is still only 25, and will certainly attract significant interest in free agency, but her restricted status means the Wings can match any offer she receives. 
The Wings committed over $1 million per year each to Smith, Shepard and Ogunbowale last offseason, but because Bueckers and Fudd are on rookie deals, they still have cap space to work with. Due to the new revenue sharing system, the exact salary cap figure for 2027 is still unclear, though we can assume it will be slightly higher than the 2026 figure of $7 million. The Wings currently have just under $5 million on the books for next season, which means they can re-sign Kuier at any cost, though doing so would limit their ability to fill out the rest of the roster unless they were able to trade one of Smith or Shepard. A congested 2027 cap sheet and less flexibility in free agency this offseason are small prices to pay to bring back a player as unique as Kuier, who is on the same timeline as Bueckers and Fudd, and retaining her should be the Wings' top priority. If that means that 2027 turns into a bridge year until Shepard and Ogunbowale's contracts are off the books (followed by Smith in 2028), that would not be the worst outcome. Especially when this group has already established itself as a playoff team and has two more first-round picks coming in this year's draft who could address some of their depth concerns, both now and in the future.  Draft outlookPicks Nos. 9, 13, 24 and 30After having the No. 1 overall pick in back-to-back drafts, the Wings will not have a lottery selection this year. They will, however, have two first-round picks -- No. 9, which is their own, and No. 13, which they got from the Las Vegas Aces via the NaLyssa Smith trade. In addition, the Wings will have two second-round picks, though those will be far less important. 
As currently constructed, the Wings have a crowded backcourt and frontcourt, but are very thin on the wing. Luckily for them, at least one of Maryland's Oluchi Okananwa or Ole Miss' Talaysia Cooper should still be on the board at No. 9. Either would be a welcome fit due to their athleticism and defensive playmaking, which would be a nice complement to the offensive skills of Bueckers and Ogunbowale. Their target at No. 13 would be more dependent on what happens in free agency. If they end up trading one of Shepard or Smith, or one of Kuier or Siegrist leaves in free agency, frontcourt depth would be a need. In that case, Chloe Kitts of South Carolina could be an option. It's also possible that the Wings don't have the roster spots or cap space to bring in two first-round picks and make a draft-and-stash selection at No. 13.

schema.headline: What's next for Wings? After Paige Bueckers' playoff debut, Dallas must shore up supporting cast - CBS Sports

title: Brent Venables blasts Oklahoma OL woes before Red River Rivalry vs. No. 1 Texas - CBS Sports
description: The Sooners coach shared regret over the 'very disappointing' offensive lineman development in his tenure, as OU
body:
The Sooners coach shared regret over the 'very disappointing' offensive lineman development in his tenure, as OU enters Saturday's matchup in Dallas dead-last in the SEC in total offense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oklahoma coach Brent Venables called out the state of the program's offensive line development ahead of a battle against No. 1 Texas on Saturday in the annual Red River Rivalry. "It's been incredibly inconsistent and very disappointing," Venables said. "As you build your football team, that's a critical place. That's a place that probably requires the most development of any position that you have on your roster." Despite retaining highly regarded offensive line coach Bill Bedenbaugh, Oklahoma's line has been among the worst in the nation for much of the past five years. The Sooners average only 2.9 yards per carry, while the offense ranks last in the SEC in total offense. According to Pro Football Focus, Oklahoma ranks No. 120 in pass blocking grade and No. 101 in run blocking grade. Venables pointed to the transfer portal as a major driver of instability at the position group, especially in the first few years after he took over the program. 
"Very uneven job when it comes to choosing the guys that we've brought in here," Venables said. "Way too many guys are coming and going at that position group. We need continuity and consistency to develop that group into what we want." 
        
            
                Is Oklahoma likely to mix it up at QB in Red River vs. Texas? Brent Venables evaluating John Mateer, options
                
                    Shehan Jeyarajah                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Broken pipelineOklahoma has long pointed to the end of the Lincoln Riley era as the primary driver behind its struggling offensive line play. The Sooners famously took only two high school offensive linemen in the Class of 2021, often cited as an indicator of deprioritization. Instead, the unit has only gotten worse under Venables. The Sooners have dropped every year in yards per carry since 2022, bottoming out at an astonishing 2.9 yards per carry this season. The unit has allowed fewer sacks since transitioning to dual-threat quarterback John Mateer, but the Sooners allowed a nation-worst 50 sacks in 2024. 
Out of five offensive line recruits in Venables' first two recruiting classes, four are no longer with the program. Three of the five recruits in the Class of 2024 have also transferred, leaving major gaps. Now, the five starters on Oklahoma's roster include two transfers (E'Marion Harris and Jake Maikkula), two underclassmen (Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje) and one upperclassman (Heath Ozaeta). Offensive tackle Michael Fasusi would also factor into the rotation, but he has missed nearly the entire season with an injury, like many other Sooners before him. Oklahoma lost six offensive linemen to the transfer portal after the 2025 season. All of them landed at Power Four schools, and four of them were named starters. Oklahoma has not turned a high school offensive line recruit into an NFL Draft pick since Anton Harrison after the 2022 season. 
Attempted investmentSince the offensive line tanked, Oklahoma has made a concerted effort to invest more heavily in it. The staff landed blue-chip recruits Fasusi and Fodje in the Class of 2025, and both have turned into contributors. However, the Sooners are hoping an incredible in-state recruiting class can further turn the tide. Oklahoma holds commits from native Oklahomans Kaeden Penny and Cooper Hackett, both rated as blue-chip recruits. The program has six commitments overall along the offensive line as part of a No. 6 national recruiting class. Between the growth of Fasusi, Fodji and Pierre-Louis and later infusion of talent, there's reason to hope that at least the pipeline is being repaired. But after five years of disaster at the position, it's fair to wonder whether the investment came too late. 
On Saturday at the State Fair of Texas, the Sooners face off against the No. 1 Longhorns. Oklahoma has been miserable against its top rival under Venables, losing three of four matchups and averaging a pathetic 3.0 points per game in the losses. Texas holds the nation's No. 5 defense in SP+, a spot ahead of Oklahoma at No. 6. They're also more than 50 spots ahead of Oklahoma in offense, leading to a Vegas line of more than 10 points. Texas defensive end Colin Simmons recorded 5.5 sacks against Tennessee and now leads the nation in sacks per game. Another putrid performance at the Cotton Bowl could spell disaster for the Venables era at Oklahoma. Unfortunately, it may be an inevitability.

        The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-1) have a running back depth issue with Zach Charbonnet not ready to go after tearing his ACL in January, and first-round rookie Jadarian Price going on injured reserve with a chest injury.That's why Seattle kicked the tires on signing two-time Pro Bowl running back Joe Mixon to its practice squad after hosting him for a workout on Monday, per ESPN. However, after a physical on Tuesday, the Seahawks reportedly opted not to sign Mixon.Mixon, who is now 30 years old, missed the entire 2025 season with a foot injury, but he ran for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns on 245 carries as the Houston Texans' bell cow back in 2024. He has run for over 1,000 yards in five of his eight career NFL seasons played, including three of his last four. 
From 2021 to 2024, with the Cincinnati Bengals and the Texans, Mixon's 4,069 yards rushing ranked as the sixth most in the league, while his 40 rushing touchdowns were tied for the fourth-most in the NFL in that span. He will now compete for snaps with veterans Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Wilson currently leads the Seahawks in carries (53), rushing yards (190 and rushing touchdowns (1) this season.

title: 2026 MLB playoffs: Which team has best chance to come back from 0-2 LDS hole? - CBS Sports
description: Three series are close to being sweeps, but which team could come back?
body:
Three series are close to being sweeps, but which team could come back?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We're now through two games in each of the four divisional series in the 2026 Major League Baseball playoffs and three of the series have a team leading two games to none. It's a best-of-five round, so three series are now on the verge of being sweeps. Of the three teams in that 2-0 hole -- the Guardians, Padres and Yankees -- which has the best shot to come back and win? Before we dive in and rank their chances, it needs to be said that it is a total long shot for any of these three teams to win. The most likely scenario is that all three lose their series. Only 10 teams have ever come back from being down 2-0 in a five-game series in MLB history, with the most recent being the 2017 Yankees. It has only happened three times since 2003.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. San Diego PadresThey used Michael King in Game 2, ran through all their big bullpen arms in the first two games and still came away with zero wins. It sure feels over. Much like when the Brewers got a runner on base and he stole second in the ninth, they feel inevitable here after a 103-win regular season and so many comebacks, not to mention winning any which way is necessary in any given game. 
On the Padres' end, they do get to return home to Petco Park, which was Vibes Central in the Wild Card Series against the Cubs. Nick Pivetta looked pretty good, and with the day off between Games 2 and 3, the Padres will have a full complement of bullpen arms available for Game 3. Win one game and you never know, right? It should also be noted that the Brewers have a drastic fall off in starting pitching after Games 1 and 2 starters Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson. While the series is very likely ending up with the Brewers, it's certainly in "you're telling me there's a chance?" range. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Cleveland GuardiansI more strongly believe in the Padres than the Guardians, but the task is different here because the Guardians are facing an 84-win regular-season team while the Padres deal with the mighty Brewers. The White Sox are a good team, but definitely not a great one. They are surviving mostly on bullpen games and have done a great job, going 4-0 in the playoffs so far. Simple logic tells us, however, that an 84-win team that has gone 4-0 in road playoff games means that, at some point, there's a regression coming, right? Of course, that regression might not come this round. The Guardians aren't exactly a juggernaut in their own right, being an 85-win regular-season team. With Parker Messick waiting in Game 4, the Guardians winning Game 3 means there would be a good chance to extend this series to Game 5. Then again, Messick started Game 1 and the Guardians lost that one. 
Further, there were six games played head-to-head between these teams in Chicago this season and the White Sox took four of six. Again, the Guardians are ranked above the Padres because they are facing a far inferior foe, but it's a major uphill battle. The most likely outcome here is that the White Sox complete the job at home. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. New York YankeesOf the three teams down 2-0, the Yankees had the best record in the regular season, along with the best run differential. They won their two Wild Card Series games over the Red Sox by a combined mark of 18-2. They have Max Fried waiting to start Game 3 here in the ALDS and will be able to go with Carlos Rodón and some combination of Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler in Game 5, should they be able to extend the series. That's a pretty darn good setup. 
Also, Fried and Rodón are lefties, and the Rays are significantly worse against left-handed pitching (.751 OPS vs. RHP, .678 vs. LHP). There's an opening here.New York's offense was broken in Tampa Bay and credit must obviously be given to the Rays' pitching staff. Going back home should help the Yankees, at least in theory. They had a .755 OPS at home and .688 on the road in the regular season. Also, while his numbers overall are very good, Rays Game 3 starter Nick Martinez had a 4.24 ERA in his last nine starts. The Yankees saw him and beat him on Sept. 22 -- though it was only 2-0 Yankees and not exactly a bloodbath. Of the three teams down 2-0, the Yankees are, in my estimation, easily the most likely to come back and win their series. They are also very likely to lose the series.

title: Jim Furyk promises changes are coming for 'underdog' Americans at 2027 Ryder Cup - CBS Sports
description: Furyk returns to Europe as the U.S. captain after serving in 2018
body:
Furyk returns to Europe as the U.S. captain after serving in 2018
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Change is required for the U.S. Ryder Cup team, and captain Jim Furyk is insistent that it is coming next year to Adare Manor in Limerick, Ireland, for the biennial event against the Europeans. At the helm for the second time in his career, Furyk has a tall task laid out in front of him as he aims to lead the Americans to victory on European soil for the first time since 1993 at The Belfry, two years after the U.S. lost on home soil at Bethpage Black."We're not real happy with the last two results, so, yes, change will be made," Furyk said. "We're going to evolve. We're going to get better, noticeably, I guess, right off the bat, a new points system moving forward, a new analytics team moving forward. But a number of different changes coming and stuff that we're very excited about."Although Furyk has not been a Ryder Cup captain since 2018, when the U.S. team lost 17.5 to 10.5 at Le Golf National near Paris, France, the 56-year-old has remained active within team leadership rooms. Furyk served as a captain in the 2024 Presidents Cup in winning fashion, as well as a vice captain in the 2025 Ryder Cup and the 2026 Presidents Cup last month at Medinah Country Club.As he noted, Furyk already implemented a new points system for the qualification process with a focus on the 2027 season.
In the last two team events, the U.S. side has dominated Sunday singles, winning the session 9.5 to 2.5 against the International team in Chicago and 8.5 to 3.5 against the Europeans at Bethpage Black the year prior. This dominance in singles has raised questions about the Americans' ability to come together in team sessions, especially in foursomes, where they have struggled and often put themselves in a hole."There's some issues. We understand that. Not something I'm very happy with. I plan on making some changes," Furyk said. "I would say, one, as captains, we need to do a better job, not only put the folks into good pairings in good positions, but I don't think we are preparing for those matches in a proper way. "And I will promise you, we will be prepared. I'm going to ask this team to do more than any other United States team has in the past. We'll be prepared. We'll be ready to go in that format, and hopefully we can showcase our talent. We have too much depth to have that poor record in alternate-shot."
At the 2023 Ryder Cup near Rome, Italy, the U.S. lost the foursomes sessions 7 to 1. At Le Golf National in 2018, they lost a combined 6 to 2. At Gleneagles in 2014, they did not win a single foursomes match and instead relied on two halves for their 7 to 1 disadvantage in the format.The U.S. has not only not won a Ryder Cup in Europe since 1993, but the red, white and blue has not come particularly close since, with only one tight contest materializing in 2010 in the form of a 14.5 to 13.5 defeat. It was in that same 2010 Ryder Cup that the U.S. last won a foursomes session in Europe. Since then, the U.S. average margin of defeat in the three Ryder Cups in Europe has been just about six points.
"We know what we're up against," Furyk said. "We also know that it's been 34 years since we won in Europe. There's no secret. I'm going to hear it over and over again, so I'm going to embrace it. You know, Luke [Donald] and Dodo [Molinari] have the opportunity to set the golf course up, trying to tip the scales to Europe. We're the underdogs. I know it's always been played, we come in, the Americans seem to be the favorites. "This year, there's no chance that that could happen. We're the underdogs. We understand that. We've got a lot of work ahead of us. And you know, I'm excited about that process. I'm a process guy and kind of ducks in a row and put these guys in a good position and let our guys go out and show their talent. It's going to be difficult…I've been saying it all week, I need 12 guys that love that atmosphere and love walking into that type of arena because it takes a certain mentality, and those are the guys I'll be looking for."

description: Holloway didn't play in the 2026 NCAA Tournament after bei
body:
Holloway didn't play in the 2026 NCAA Tournament after being arrested on felony drug charges
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Alabama star guard Aden Holloway will be suspended for three exhibition games against Furman, Ole Miss and Auburn, and the first two games of the 2026-27 season against Sam Houston and Arkansas State, Al.com reported on Tuesday. Holloway entered the Tuscaloosa County District Attorney's "second chance" program as part of his plea agreement following two felony drug charges earlier this summer.Holloway was eligible for the "second chance" program because he was a first-time offender with non-violent felonies. The program includes random drug testing, 50 hours of community service and educational courses. Holloway didn't play in the 2026 NCAA Tournament after being suspended from campus following the charges. The Crimson Tide reached the Sweet 16 without Holloway after picking up wins over Hofstra and Texas Tech before losing to eventual national champion Michigan.
        
            
                Alabama's Aden Holloway enters 'second chance' program and offers apology letter after felony drug charges
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"We were disappointed by the choices Aden made, but we have been encouraged by the way he has responded," Alabama athletic director Greg Byrne told Al.com.Holloway averaged 16.8 points, 3.8 assists and 2.8 rebounds during his second season with the Crimson Tide after transferring from Auburn in 2024. He finished as Alabama's second-leading scorer behind star guard Labaron Philon Jr. and will be able to be reinstated for his team's third game of the season against Oakland on Nov. 9. 
The Crimson Tide opens the season against Sam Houston on Nov. 3.

title: Chargers fire sale at NFL trade deadline? Landing spots for Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu - CBS Sports
description: A disastrous start could force Los Angeles to move expiring contracts ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
body:
A disastrous start could force Los Angeles to move expiring contracts ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Chargers are arguably the biggest disappointment of the 2026 NFL season. After back-to-back 11-6 seasons under Jim Harbaugh, the Chargers enter the month of October still looking for their first victory. They have started 0-4 for the first time since 2017, and are just the third team in NFL history to start 0-4 after back-to-back 11-win seasons. The Chargers were viewed as the sleeper in the AFC West after hiring former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel to be their new offensive coordinator. However, Los Angeles currently ranks fourth-worst in scoring offense (16.8 points per game) and 12th-worst in total offense (306.8 total yards per game), while Justin Herbert hasn't been playing like a franchise quarterback. He's completing a career-low 59.7% of his passes for a career-low 204.0 passing yards per game with four touchdowns and six interceptions. It's been a disaster.With games against the Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs and Los Angeles Rams next up on the docket, it's fair to wonder when that first victory is coming for the Chargers. We are in dangerous territory of this becoming a lost season for Harbaugh, as the Chargers' Over/Under win total at DraftKings Sportsbook is currently listed at 5.5. If things continue to go downhill for Los Angeles, the Chargers could be sellers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. They have a few intriguing trade targets teams will be looking at -- especially when it comes to pass rusher. Let's take a look at some Chargers players who could be traded in the near future, and a couple of potential landing spots for them as well.
EDGE Khalil MackVeteran pass rusher Khalil Mack is now 35 years old and playing on an expiring deal. A contender should reach out and see what it costs to acquire the former NFL Defensive Player of the Year.Mack has actually recorded three sacks in his first four games this season to go along with 14 tackles and 13 pressures. He is just three years removed from his last double-digit sack season, recording a career-high 17 QB takedowns in 2023.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wouldn't it be something if Mack returned to the Chicago Bears, where he spent four seasons from 2018-2021? He made three straight Pro Bowls in Chicago and recorded 36 sacks in 53 games played. 
The Bears have Montez Sweat, Austin Booker and Dayo Odeyingbo -- who leads the team with three sacks. Pass rusher is not the biggest need on the team, but a Mack homecoming would help boost Chicago's defense as the Bears look to repeat as NFC North champions.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    The San Francisco 49ers are tied in having the best record in the NFL at 4-0, but have the most games missed due to injury with 76, according to CBS Sports Research. That includes Nick Bosa, who is expected to miss multiple weeks due to a calf injury, and Mykel Williams, who is on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. The 49ers rank in the bottom six in the NFL in sacks with six, as Keion White leads the way with two QB takedowns. John Lynch would be smart to upgrade at pass rusher. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    We could see new Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter push to acquire one of his former players in Mack. Trey Hendrickson, Tavius Robinson and Mike Green headline the Ravens' pass-rush group, but it could be better. Baltimore has recorded seven sacks over four games, which ranks in the bottom 10. 
The Ravens ranked bottom four in sacks last year, which led them to sign Hendrickson. He's managed just one sack in three games played, and recently underwent surgery on his finger. Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz knows the Ravens organization as well, as he spent 25+ years there working in player personnel and scouting.EDGE Tuli TuipulotuWhile some NFL teams are focused on Khalil Mack, there are others who could be interested in the Chargers' other pass rusher: Tuli Tuipulotu. He made the Pro Bowl last year after racking up a career-high 13 sacks to go along with 20 tackles for loss. It was thought he was holding in for a new deal this preseason, since Tuipulotu is set to make less than $6 million in 2026, but he's been on the field. Tuipulotu has recorded 18 tackles, two sacks, two passes defensed and one interception in four games played this year. The Chargers front office has likely already spent some time negotiating with Tuipulotu's camp, so they have some idea whether a long-term extension is in the cards. If it's not, it makes sense to acquire draft capital rather than lose a starting pass rusher for nothing. The Chargers did spend a first-round pick on a pass rusher in this past draft with Akheem Mesidor.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tuipulotu just had a fantastic game against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, recording six tackles, half a sack, his first career interception and one forced fumble. If he were to join the Seahawks, Tuipulotu could come in and immediately join a fun rotation, then get paid and take on a starting role when DeMarcus Lawrence and Dante Fowler Jr. leave this upcoming offseason.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    This seems like a Howie Roseman trade. Acquire an underrated pass rusher that is due for a raise, and give him an opportunity to flourish. The Philadelphia Eagles are tied for 31st in sacks this season with four. This Vic Fangio defense as a whole has disappointed, but there's concern for this pass rush. Nolan Smith Jr. is actually the only pass rusher who has gotten to the quarterback this season! 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    The soon-to-be 84-year-old Jerry Jones is swinging trades left and right for the Dallas Cowboys. He acquired pass rusher Rashan Gary in the offseason, and just made a move for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. last week. Could he continue to wheel-and-deal by scooping Tuipulotu? Despite all of the moves the Cowboys have made, this defense is still struggling. That goes for the pass rush as well, which is tied with the Eagles, Dolphins and Chiefs in having the second-fewest sacks in the NFL this year. As we enter Week 5, the Cowboys rank bottom five in both total defense and scoring defense.
Who else could be moved?Wide receiver Quentin Johnston had a career year in 2025 with 735 yards receiving and eight touchdowns on 51 receptions. However, he's caught just seven passes for 108 yards and zero touchdowns through four games this season. What could make Johnston tough to move is that the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option for 2027, meaning he will make $18 million fully guaranteed. Maybe there's an interested team out there that will consider giving him a multi-year extension. There are plenty of teams looking for help at cornerback, and the veteran Donte Jackson could be a potential trade target since he's on an expiring deal. Jackson is in his second season with the Chargers, and has recorded eight tackles and two passes defensed with one forced fumble through Week 4.Tight end David Njoku is currently on injured reserve, but he could potentially be a sneaky trade target at the deadline. We don't know the extent of his injury, but in the best-case scenario, he could hypothetically return Nov. 1 if the injury isn't long-term. Njoku caught just six passes for 67 yards in his two games with the Chargers, but was an athletic weapon during his nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns. If Njoku is not seriously injured, perhaps a team would be interested in acquiring him for cheap next month.

The South Carolina coach says he's shutting out speculation on his future as he tries to improve his team following a 2-3 start

        There's no quieting the noise surrounding Shane Beamer's future at South Carolina, but the struggling Gamecocks' coach understands the scrutiny as the leader of an SEC program and says he is working to get things corrected this season.South Carolina's 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky over the weekend was the team's eighth straight in the SEC and 12th setback in its last 14 games against Power Four opponents.Few coaches are facing the amount of pressure that Beamer's under right now, but he doesn't seem worried about his status heading into a Week 6 showdown at Florida."It's a challenge. It is what it is. It's week to week in this league and I know that. Right now, 2-3 is not good enough," Beamer said Tuesday. "I haven't been good enough as a head coach. I own it. We've got to get better as a football team. It really doesn't change, going into it versus in it. Right now, I'm focusing on what I can control, and that's trying to put together the best team to go play on Saturdays to give us the best chance to be successful on Saturdays.
"All I can go on is the conversations I've had with (athletic director) Jeremiah (Donati), (senior deputy director of athletics) Jeff Crane, and the text message I got from our president emeritus over the weekend -- who's been awesome. Some of our biggest donors that I've gotten phone calls, voicemails and text messages … that's why I go on, not what people and their 'sources' say. Then it doesn't happen, and suddenly it's, 'well, my sources now say this. "It's like c'mon man."Recent social media comments about his job on a post centered on his daughter's senior night at her high school, the night before South Carolina's loss to Mississippi State, really bothered Beamer."There's some crappy people in the world, there just is," Beamer said, who is currently on a three-week break from checking his phone, he confirmed.
CBS Sports reported on Monday that Beamer's job security isn't as tenuous as it seems due to financial constraints at the university.Beamer has mentioned the support he has from the school's administration several times during this current three-game slide and said as much during Tuesday's press conference."I don't know if social media is always real-life," Beamer said. "What you see on social media vs. what is actually real. I know the noise out there last week versus what was actually real.
"The same people in the student section against Mississippi State, chanting 'Fire Beamer' at the end of the game, seven days earlier, they were screaming 'Beamer Ball' at the end of the game when we beat Towson. It's truly week to week."Dylan Stewart returns to practice, availability TBAAfter a week away from the program, defensive end Dylan Stewart has returned to team activities. Last week, Stewart served his one-game suspension from the SEC for striking an Alabama player in the Gamecocks' loss to the Crimson Tide. In addition to punishment from the conference, Stewart is currently on an indefinite suspension from Beamer. "He came back today and was in the 8 a.m. team meeting we had this morning, and he was at practice," Beamer said. "As I've told him and the team, his status will be determined as we go throughout the week."
Stewart was a five-star recruit in the Class of 2024 and one of the most significant recruits of the Beamer era at South Carolina. The junior posted a combined 22.5 tackles for loss and 11 sacks in his first two seasons with the program.He has yet to record a sack over two games as he works his way back from injury."I do believe my job as the head coach is to win football games, but it's also to help young men and help them grow," Beamer said. "Last week was a learning lesson from him and I (hope) there was growth from that. He's a good young man that I care a lot about. He's not, and I'm not condoning his actions in Tuscaloosa at all, and it's unacceptable, but he's not the first person that has ever punched a player in a game, and he won't be the last."

title: Yankees facing elimination: The changes Aaron Boone must make before Game 3 vs. Rays - CBS Sports
description: New York played an embarrassing brand of baseball in Games 1 and 2 and now must rebound at home in Game 3 to keep
body:
New York played an embarrassing brand of baseball in Games 1 and 2 and now must rebound at home in Game 3 to keep its season alive
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first two games of the ALDS could not have gone much worse for the New York Yankees. They were no-hit into the eighth inning by Tampa Bay Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in Game 1, then they played Little League-level defense in Game 2. It was an embarrassing display of baseball from a team that has had a knack for embarrassing displays the last few postseasons.   "Obviously, a really rough night to say the least for us," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after Game 2. "We've got to get over it.  We've responded all year to difficult times, and we've got to do that again.  We've got to get ourselves up off the mat."   Only 10 times has a team rallied from a 2-0 deficit to win a best-of-five series. In the 2-2-1 Division Series format, there have been only three comebacks in 36 instances of a team falling behind 2-0 on the road. The last team to do it? Aaron Judge's 2017 Yankees against Cleveland. Judge, left off the ALDS roster due to injury, and the front office are the only shared link between the 2017 and 2026 Yankees, however.   
        
            
                Which team has the best chance to come back from its 2-0 Division Series hole: Guardians, Padres or Yankees?
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"It starts one play, one inning at a time," Boone said. "We can't play like that and expect a win. We've got to come out Wednesday night, everything's on the line. It's obviously all hands on deck, and we've got to try and get one. And then go from there. We're capable of doing it. This team has been really good at picking themselves up all year."
What do the Yankees need to do to erase this 2-0 deficit and beat the Rays in the Division Series? Here are four things that must happen for the Yankees to avoid a second straight ALDS defeat, beginning with Wednesday night's Game 3 in the Bronx.   1. Max Fried and Carlos Rodón must be great   Pitching hasn't really been an issue for the Yankees in the ALDS. Two games into the series, the Rays are hitting .209/.261/.313, and three of their six runs are unearned. New York's pitching, specifically Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler, has been solid enough, but the Yankees will need it to be better than that to force a Game 4, never mind complete the 2-0 comeback.    Three teams have lost Games 1 and 2 on the road and rallied to win the Division Series in the 2-2-1 format era. The common theme is a great Game 3 start:  
Game 3 SPSeriesIPHRBBKMasahiro Tanaka, Yankees 				 				 				 				 				2017 ALDS vs. Cleveland 				 				 				 				 				7 				 				 				 				 				3 				 				 				 				 				0 				 				 				 				 				1 				 				 				 				 				7 				 				 				 				 				Derek Lowe, Red Sox 				 				 				 				 				2003 ALDS vs. Athletics 				 				 				 				 				7 				 				 				 				 				6 				 				 				 				 				1 				 				 				 				 				2 				 				 				 				 				2 				 				 				 				 				Ramon Martinez, Red Sox 				 				 				 				 				1999 ALDS vs. Cleveland 				 				 				 				 				5 ⅔ 				 				 				 				 				5 				 				 				 				 				2 				 				 				 				 				3 				 				 				 				 				6 				 				 				 				 				Max Fried, who threw six shutout innings in his Wild Card Series start, will start Game 3 on Wednesday. Carlos Rodón will start a potential Game 4 on Thursday. He was New York's second-best starter behind Schlittler the final two months of the regular season. Fried and Rodón bode particularly well because the Rays have struggled against lefties this year.Here are Tampa's platoon splits since the Aug. 3rd trade deadline. The numbers since that date better reflect the lineup you'll see in the ALDS than the team's full-season numbers:    Rays vs. RHPRays vs. LHPBatting average 				 				.265 				 				.246 				 				On-base percentage 				 				.326 				 				.311 				 				Slugging percentage 				 				.427 				 				.354 				 				Series comebacks always start with the guy on the mound and on paper, Fried and Rodón match up well with the Rays. They are two high-end veteran lefties who would not be out of place starting Games 1 and 2 in the postseason (they did that just last year for the Yankees). The Yankees will have the right guys on the mound in Games 3 and 4.    2. Get some righties in the lineup  The Yankees have used the same starting lineup in their last three postseason games and that lineup included eight left-handed batters. Rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. was the only righty. This has been their go-to postseason lineup:  DH Ben Rice, LHBLF Cody Bellinger, LHB1B Luis García Jr., LHBCF Spencer Jones, LHBSS George Lombard Jr., RHB2B Jazz Chisholm Jr., LHBCF Trent Grisham, LHBC Austin Wells, LHB3B Ryan McMahon, LHBPitchers sometimes talk about "lanes" for their pitches, such as the inside corner for fastballs or down-and-away for changeups. I can't help but wonder if the eight-lefty lineup has made it easy for Tampa's pitchers to lock into their lanes and stay in their lanes. There is no lineup balance. No need to change lanes and adjust your approach because almost every hitter is left-handed.  The Yankees are carrying six bench players this series and all six hit right-handed. They shouldn't make wholesale changes and run out a righty-heavy lineup in Game 3 -- Tampa is starting righty Nick Martinez on Wednesday -- but working in another righty or two seems worthwhile at this point. Realistically, the Yankees have five options to do this:José Caballero for McMahon (0 for 3 in the ALDS)Paul Goldschmidt for García (0 for 7 in the ALDS)Anthony Volpe for Chisholm (0 for 6 in the ALDS)Heliot Ramos for Grisham (0 for 6 in the ALDS) or Jones (0 for 7 in the ALDS)Goldschmidt is best used in moderation at this point in his career. He's a platoon bat and not someone I would look to get into the lineup against a righty with the season on the line. García may be 0 for 7 in the ALDS, but he hit 30 home runs during the regular season, and he can change the game with one swing in a way Goldschmidt can't this late in his career.  The other potential moves all fall into the "well, we have to do something" bucket. Other than maybe Caballero over McMahon, none of those moves are clear-cut upgrades. Ramos is a poor defender who, like Goldschmidt, is a platoon guy against lefties. Volpe was banished to the minors twice this year and has been one of the worst hitters in baseball since his debut in 2023.  I think it's worth going Caballero over McMahon and Ramos over either Grisham or Jones (I'd swap out Jones given his extreme strikeout tendencies) in Game 3. These (probably) aren't season-saving moves, but they would at least add balance to an offense that has gone stale the last two games, and simply has too many unproductive left-handed hitters.  Also worth noting: Martinez allowed a .704 OPS to righties and a .660 OPS to lefties in 2026.  3. Use home-field advantage  Tropicana Field has been a House of Horrors for the Yankees for some time now. They are 2-7 at the Trop this season and 7-14 there since 2023. Similar to the Yankees and Yankee Stadium's short right field porch, the Rays are built for Tropicana Field's turf. They use it and their speed to pressure defenses and get them to unravel like the Yankees did in Game 2.  The Yankees had an even home/road split this season. They went 46-34 with a plus-58 run differential at home and 47-34 with a plus-80 run differential on the road. The Rays, meanwhile, were significantly better at home. That isn't to say they were bad on the road. They just weren't as dominant.    W-LRun differentialRays at home 				 				55-26 				 				+51 				 				Rays on road 				 				43-38 				 				+35 				 				In a recent ESPN poll, managers and coaches voted Yankee Stadium the most intimidating postseason ballpark of the eight Division Series teams. It's loud and the atmosphere is electric. The Yankees need that home-field advantage in Games 3 and 4 to have any chance at pushing this series back to Tropicana Field for a potential Game 5.    4. Get a little lucky  With their backs up against the wall, the Yankees need every little break. Getting a favorable call on a borderline pitch in a big spot (and hope the ABS challenge goes your way). A bloop off the end of the bat landing just fair (or foul). A good defender booting a play. It is better to be lucky than good, but to beat the Rays three straight times, the Yankees will need to be lucky and good. There's no shame in asking the baseball gods for a little help.     "We've got to play the first inning of Game 3.  We've got to come out and play well," Boone said after Game 2. "We've responded all year.  We need to do it again.  Obviously, we need to play better and it starts with just one at a time.  I don't even get ahead of myself and (try to) win three.  We've got to go win one and we've got to play better Wednesday night to make that happen."

        Michigan tight end Zack Marshall has issued an apology on social media for comments critical of his team's offense and its usage of tight ends following Saturday's mistake-filled loss to Minnesota."Last weekend, in the hours after we lost, I made some inappropriate comments that I regret," Marshall posted Tuesday. "The game is won and lost as a team, and I pointed fingers instead of taking accountability. I let my frustrations speak for me in an emotional moment. I apologize to my teammates and coaches for the unnecessary drama that this has caused."Marshall, a senior without a catch this season, allegedly wrote in a leaked text message that Michigan offensive coordinator Jason Beck, "had a meeting with all the [tight ends] and told us none of us are valuable to this offense."Marshall had 16 receptions for 199 yards and a touchdown last fall for the Wolverines, but has played behind Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman this season. As a team, only nine of Michigan's 69 completed passes have gone to tight ends so far this year.
A Michigan spokesperson told ESPN this week that the Wolverines' coaching staff is aware of the situation and has met with Marshall about his choice of words.Kyle Whittingham is struggling out of the gate in Year 1 as the Wolverines are 3-2 overall, including an 0-2 start to Big Ten play.The veteran coach told reporters that something has to change on offense for a team that's scored 19 and 14 points each of its last two games, both losses against league competition.
"Obviously, we had many offensive woes in this past game," he said Tuesday. "We were not nearly as productive as we needed to be, really, at anything. Didn't run the ball well enough, didn't throw it well enough, weren't good on third down, didn't protect the quarterback like we needed to. We turned it over. Just a myriad of issues that we gotta deal with, and it was discouraging in the respect that we had really taken a step forward each week with the offense up until last week, and we regressed, and so we've got our work cut out for us."Michigan ranks 17th in the Big Ten in total offense, 17th in scoring offense and last in explosive plays.It was supposed to come much easier this season for Underwood in his second campaign as the Wolverines' starter under a playcaller who saw immense success with his quarterbacks at Utah in 2025.
"Offensively, we've got a long way to go," Whittingham said. "I'm telling you right now, there's a lot of issues, and we gotta address them. It's just a situation of, again, figuring out what have we done well so far. What do we need to just cast off and not try to do anymore, try to put a square peg in a round hole, and find a way to manage the game offensively so we have a chance to win."

title: NFL Referees Association to challenge officials' suspensions for Week 4 conduct - CBS Sports
description: Referee Adrian Hill and line judge Jeff Seeman both face suspensions for 'unprofessional conduct'
body:
Referee Adrian Hill and line judge Jeff Seeman both face suspensions for 'unprofessional conduct'
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL had gone eight years without issuing a suspension to a single official before it suspended referee Adrian Hill and line judge Jeff Seeman for their conduct during their Week 4 assignments. The NFL Referees Association said it disagrees with the rare punishment the league handed down and will challenge the severity of both suspensions. Hill faces a one-game ban while Seeman is set to miss two games.The union argues that the suspensions for unprofessional conduct stretch beyond appropriate punishment. History, to an extent, sides with the union in Seeman's case in particular. His two-game suspension is the longest for an official since 1988, and officials previously suspended for altercations with players each sat just one game."NFL officials have a responsibility to conduct themselves professionally on the field, and the actions in these incidents fell short of that standard," NFLRA executive director Scott Green said in a statement. "Accountability matters, but that should not result in discipline that is excessive or inconsistent with established precedent."A league review of Seeman's interaction with Trey McBride determined that the line judge used profanity at the Arizona Cardinals tight end. McBride initially pleaded for a pass interference penalty he thought should have been called on a third-down incompletion. CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala said McBride was heated in his plea for a penalty flag but did not use vulgar language toward the official.
NFL Players Association president JC Tretter released a statement regarding that play and called for the league to hold officials to the "same standard" as players.
Hill's suspension stems from an incident with Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson. Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II inadvertently shoved Wilson into the referee, who then fell backward to the ground. Wilson saw the referee tumble and extended his arms to help him up, but instead of taking the assistance, Hill stood up under his own power and began yelling at Wilson.
"Officials are routinely subjected to highly charged interactions and, at times, verbal abuse from players and coaches," Green said. "While that never excuses misconduct by an official, it shouldn't be dismissed as simply part of the game. The League expects the highest level of professionalism from its officials, and it should demand the same from everyone on the field."Confrontations between officials and players seem to be on the rise. The NFLRA said it plans to meet with the NFLPA leadership team to address the matter and intends to meet with the league's officiating department to discuss disciplinary standards.
"We will defend the principle that discipline must be fair, consistent and proportionate," Green said. "Holding officials accountable while ignoring or minimizing the conduct directed at them is neither fair nor an effective way to address this issue."

title: Ranking NFL division leaders by most vulnerable teams after opening month: Browns a fraud? - CBS Sports
description: Now that the first month of the 2026 regular season is over and done, you might have an urge to go look at the standings throughout the
body:
Now that the first month of the 2026 regular season is over and done, you might have an urge to go look at the standings throughout the league to see where everyone stacks up. When you do, let me be the first to tell you that you don't need to clean your glasses and your eyes aren't deceiving you. There are some surprising division leaders through the first four weeks. I mean, if you had the Cleveland Browns atop the AFC North at any point this year, I would like to ask you a few questions. Specifically, I'd like you to tell me this week's winning lottery numbers, since you clearly can see the future. Meanwhile, the New York Giants are another club that is remarkably leading it's division, the NFC East. That wouldn't be surprising if Jaxson Dart was still their starting quarterback, but it certainly is after he went down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, which has thrust Jameis Winston under center. Here, we're going to sift through these leaders and determine which have staying power and which are merely visiting the top spot before making the trek down. To do that, we'll rank all eight first-place teams from the least vulnerable to losing their spot (No. 8) down to the most vulnerable (No. 1).  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1)Odds to win AFC South: -250Jacksonville is sitting pretty atop the AFC South, and the betting odds support that. The Jaguars are currently the biggest favorite to win their division in the entire NFL, and it's easy to see why. While there are still some undefeated teams across the league, the Jaguars have the makings of a true threat to come out of the AFC. They just went into Cincinnati and beat the Bengals, which continues a white-hot run that dates back to last season. Over its past 12 regular-season games, Jacksonville is 11-1, averaging 31.1 points and allowing just 14.1.
 As much as this is a credit to Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence forming quite the head coach-QB pairing, it also speaks to the lackluster nature of the rest of the division. Both the Texans and Titans are 0-4 to begin the year. Houston's offensive line continues to disappoint, and its defense has even regressed a bit from last season, so it doesn't appear to be a legitimate threat. Neither does Tennessee, as it appears destined to have another top-five pick at the NFL Draft. The most competitive division rival appears to be the Colts at 2-2, but even they don't strike fear into true playoff contenders. Daniel Jones doesn't look like the same quarterback he was in the first half of last year before his Achilles injury, and the defense is giving up the second-most total yards in the NFL through four weeks. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0)Odds to win AFC West: -225Kansas City has jumped right back into being one of the elite teams in the AFC, with Patrick Mahomes largely not skipping a beat in his return from a torn ACL and LCL last season. The free-agent addition of Kenneth Walker III has also given the offense some much-needed explosiveness and has been a key catalyst for the 4-0 start to the season. K.C. is another division leader that is becoming an overwhelming favorite to keep its grip on the crown, especially after taking down the previously undefeated Raiders in Week 3. While Las Vegas began the year 3-0 and is building a solid foundation under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak, it still feels a year or two away from truly making a push in the division. As for the Denver Broncos, they, in theory, are the biggest challenger to the Chiefs after making the AFC Championship Game last season. However, the offense has been plagued by slow starts throughout the first month, and Bo Nix ranks 19th out of 24 qualified quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. For reference, Mahomes ranks eighth. Even the Denver defense, which is supposed to be the team's strength, ranks 20th in the league in yards allowed per play (5.6). Meanwhile, the Chargers at 0-4 are a virtual non-factor. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. San Francisco 49ers (4-0)Odds to win NFC West: +100San Francisco plays in the toughest division in the NFL, so putting it this low in terms of being vulnerable should tell you how good it has been through four weeks. Yes, the 49ers will have to fend off the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks and the still-current betting favorite to win Super Bowl LXI in the Rams, but they have the nucleus to do it. The Niners already beat the Rams in a head-to-head in Australia in the season opener and have jumped out to a 4-0 record. Seattle is right behind at 3-1, and these two square off against one another in Week 5, so either San Francisco can post two marquee division wins over the first five weeks or find itself momentarily looking up at the Seahawks due to the tiebreaker. When you look at the advanced metrics with the 49ers, it's hard not to have confidence in them. Offensively, they've run the lowest percentage of plays that lose yards at 2.2% (excluding kneels) by any team through four games since 2000. Defensively, they're giving up the lowest percentage of explosive plays (3.5%) by any team through four games since 2000. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked. 
If they can keep this level of play up (or even keep it relatively close to these figures), they should win the requisite games to win the NFC West. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Buffalo Bills (3-1)Odds to win AFC East: -215Buffalo has better odds than the 49ers to win the division, but it's hard to ignore the fact that it just lost a pivotal early-season matchup to the Patriots in Week 4. Despite New England's rocky start, that win brought it to 2-2 on the season and within striking range of Buffalo, especially after securing the first head-to-head of the season on the road. The Patriots' schedule also softens up over the next month-plus, so Buffalo will need to be careful not to slip up. That puts an ever greater emphasis on what is slated to be a tough matchup in Week 5 as the Bills travel to Los Angeles to face the Rams on Monday night. Another element that the Bills shouldn't ignore is that they'll be on the road for a large portion of the second half of the season, specifically down the final stretch. Of their final six games, four will be on the road. While trips to New England and Denver (on Christmas) could be daunting, the Packers currently don't look like a major threat, and the other road trip is to Miami to face a Dolphins team that'll likely be more interested in draft position than anything else. 
As for the Jets, they've been pesky through the first few weeks of the season, but they don't pose a real threat to Buffalo in the division race, so it's really only New England the Bills need to concern themselves with. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Carolina Panthers (2-2)Odds to win NFC South: +160Carolina is technically knotted up with the Falcons for the NFC South lead, but currently edges them out thanks to the head-to-head victory from Week 2. The Panthers have flashed their potential at times this season, particularly with Bryce Young. The former No. 1 overall pick leads the NFL in passing yards this season, and his nine passing touchdowns are the most through the first four games of a season in franchise history. They'll be on the bye in Week 5, so the next time they take the field will be in Week 6 when they travel to Philadelphia to face the Eagles. They'll look to get over .500 for the first time this season and will have a solid rest advantage. Not only will Carolina be coming off its bye, but the Eagles will also be returning from an international game in London against the Jaguars in Week 5. 
While Carolina's offense has flashed, its defense still has some questions, allowing the fourth-most total yards per game in the NFL. It's also the seventh-worst red-zone defense (72.7%) in the league. The biggest challenger for the division crown will likely be the Falcons. That initial victory over Atlanta came with Cooper Rush at quarterback for the Falcons. With Michael Penix Jr. back, the Falcons are 2-0 and averaging 40 points per game. They'll come back down to earth in some capacity, but they could be a thorn in their side. New Orleans has talent, but it is 1-3 through the first month and was just walloped by the Falcons, so it still has work to do before we truly consider it a threat to the Panthers. Meanwhile, the Bucs are 0-4 and Baker Mayfield is sidelined with a thumb injury. The Panthers are tied for the third-easiest remaining strength of schedule in the NFL, so there is a path to repeating as NFC South champions, but they'll need to keep an eye on the Falcons.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Minnesota Vikings (4-0)Odds to win NFC North: +125The Vikings are surprisingly one of just three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. That can be credited to the stellar play on the defensive side of the ball, as they are allowing just 262.8 total yards per game. That's the third-fewest allowed during a 4-0 start to a season by any team since 1940. They remained undefeated even as their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, missed time due to a concussion. They have since gotten Murray back, and that raises concerns about their staying power at the top of the division. The veteran doesn't look like a great fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense. Over his past two starts, he has completed 63.6% of his passes, averaging 207.5 passing yards per game, one touchdown and one interception. He's also rushed for 33 yards on eight total attempts. That's fine, but it's not out of this world either, as he has a passer rating of just 80.1. At some point, the defense isn't going to be able to simply shut down their opponents en route to a win. It'll have to be the offense living up to its promise of being a high-powered unit with a capable quarterback under center. I'm not totally confident they'll answer the bell. Moreover, I think the Chicago Bears are the class of this division and are hot on the heels of Minnesota at 3-1. Yes, the Vikings have the head-to-head tiebreaker currently, thanks to a Week 2 win, but that was the game where Chicago lost Caleb Williams due to a hamstring injury. The Bears have stayed afloat with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent at quarterback, owning a 2-0 record over the past two weeks, and Williams should be back on the field soon. 
While the Lions and Packers are both 2-2 and have clear weaknesses, there is the possibility that one or both rebound. For Detroit, it hopes to get reinforcements for a depleted secondary with safety Brian Branch on the mend and possibly fellow safety Kerby Joseph. With the Packers, star pass rusher Micah Parsons could return in the coming weeks as well, and that could change their defense overnight. Those are wild cards that could flip the division that Minnesota will need to monitor on top of Chicago. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. New York Giants (3-1)Odds to win NFC East: +500New York was a sleeper candidate to win the NFC East coming into the season after John Harbaugh was hired as head coach and with Jaxson Dart entering Year 2. After defeating the Dallas Cowboys in the season opener, it looked as if the Giants would be well on their way. However, with Dart going down with a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, it has changed the complexion of the season. Jameis Winston has been able to keep them afloat over the past two weeks, but those wins were against the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals, who are expected to have some of the worst records in the league by season's end. New York's schedule isn't daunting, but with a backup quarterback like Winston (or J.J. McCarthy), no game is guaranteed, which opens the doors for division rivals. Dallas is currently the betting favorite to win the division at +134 and does feel like the most complete team in the NFC East at the moment. The offense is tied for the second-highest scoring unit in the league, averaging 30.5 points per game. The Cowboys are also the fourth-best on third down (51.02%) and the third-best in the league in the red zone (81.25%) through the first month. Their defense is still a major question, but the addition of corner Joey Poerter Jr. should help improve the secondary. 
After Dallas, the Eagles possess the best odds to win the NFC East at +140. Philadelphia has been plagued by injuries as DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, and Dallas Goedert have all been dinged up at times. That said, if it can get healthy, it arguably has the most talent of any team in the division. With Washington, it needs to focus on getting Jayden Daniels (left elbow) healthy. If he can return and improve the 1-3 record, then we can look at the Commanders as a threat, but we're still a ways away from that. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Cleveland Browns (3-1)Odds to win AFC North: +1100After Cleveland lost by 24 points to the Jaguars in Week 1, it looked like the Browns would be in for a dreadful season. However, they've since won three straight, which included a massive win over the Steelers in Pittsburgh in Week 4. That has them in first place in the AFC North after the first month, but the oddsmakers aren't exactly buying this resurgence. Cleveland is +1100 to win the AFC North, which is by far the longest among the current division leaders. The Ravens are -170, while Cincinnati is +235. The only team Cleveland is ahead of is the Steelers, who are +1150 to win the division. Baltimore and Cincinnati, on paper, are both more talented than the Browns and have an immensely higher ceiling at quarterback. While Deshaun Watson has played well during this winning streak, his off-target rate is the seventh-highest among 24 qualified quarterbacks, and his four dropped-interception rate leads the league. With both games against the Ravens and Bengals still upcoming on the schedule, this early-season run by Cleveland could be short-lived.

title: How Michael Penix Jr. has maximized Falcons' offense - CBS Sports
description: The Falcons are leading the league in scoring over the last two weeks with Penix, but the question remains whethe
body:
The Falcons are leading the league in scoring over the last two weeks with Penix, but the question remains whether this is real or a mirage
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 6, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Through the first two weeks of the season, the Atlanta Falcons were the worst offense in the NFL. They scored just 16 total points and did not enter the red zone even once during those two games. Over the last two weeks, the Falcons have led the NFL with 80 total points. They dropped 35 on the Green Bay Packers on "Thursday Night Football" and 45 on the New Orleans Saints on "Monday Night Football."Atlanta's Bijan Robinson-led run game has exploded in those two contests, totaling 447 yards on the ground. Robinson and No. 2 back Brian Robinson tagged the Packers for 242 yards and the Saints for 205. They also ran pretty well in the first two games (120 yards against the Pittsburgh Steelers and 157 against the Carolina Panthers), but it's been an entirely different level in Weeks 3 and 4.However, the main difference between the first two games and the latter two: The Falcons replaced backup quarterback Cooper Rush with starter Michael Penix Jr. starting in Week 3. Rush was dreadful in the first two games, while Penix has largely played well through his two starts. Through four weeks of the season, there are 41 quarterbacks who have thrown at least 30 passes, according to Tru Media. Rush ranks 41st among that group in expected points added (EPA) per dropback, while Penix checks in fifth. Needless to say, Penix has completely rejuvenated the Falcons' offense. It's worth investigating what he has brought to the offensive attack that Rush couldn't.
How Penix has changed the offenseLet's start with what's been the same. Penix and Rush have both gotten the ball out extremely quickly. Rush's average time to throw, per Tru Media, was 2.53 seconds, which was fourth-quickest among the aforementioned 41 passers. Penix is getting the ball out even faster, at 2.36 seconds, which is the fastest in the league to date.A lot of that is because both players have thrown many screens. Rush was 7-of-8 on screens through his two starts, while Penix is 8-of-9. That means screens accounted for 20.5% of Rush's pass attempts and 20% of Penix's. Through the first four weeks of the year, Rush and Penix rank first and second among the 41 qualified quarterbacks for passes that were thrown at or behind the line of scrimmage. They're both being schemed for easy completions.The difference is that Penix has actually opened up some of the stuff farther down the field. Just 23% of Rush's passes traveled more than 10 yards in the air, per Tru Media. That number is 31.1% for Penix. Rush went only 3-of-9 for 56 yards on those pass attempts, while Penix is 9-of-14 for 276 yards and a touchdown. 
Penix has also shown an ability to hit the wide sides of the ball that Rush couldn't access. On throws more than 5 air yards outside the numbers, Rush was just 3-of-5 for 55 yards, per Tru Media. Penix is already 9-of-13 for 213 yards and a score. He's connected repeatedly with Drake London on these types of plays, whether on sail routes, double moves or go balls. It's allowed London to run into open space or use his big body to box out the defensive back and make a play downfield.
How Penix has helped rushing attack, play actionBeing able to make these types of throws also helps the run game, as teams are less willing to devote extra men to the box to stop the rushing attack. Atlanta's rushing success rate with seven or more defenders in the box was just 27% through the first two weeks of the season, third-worst in the league, per Tru Media. In Weeks 3 and 4, that figure spiked to 63.6%, the highest in the NFL.Perhaps because of that, the Falcons have utilized play action far more often with Penix (20 dropbacks) than Rush (5). Penix is 13-of-20 for 259 yards and a touchdown on those plays, and two of the incompletions were drops. He's thrown deep 15% of the time and created eight 10-plus-yard completions and seven of 20-plus yards. It's been highly effective.
Can Penix continue his hot start?The question, of course, is whether this can keep up. And that's definitely a question. Penix was tasked with making a lot of the same types of throws during his first two seasons, but he was much less effective. He completed only 59.6% of his passes at an average of 7.2 yards per attempt. He got the ball out quickly and often threw to the sidelines and the intermediate-to-deep areas of the field, but he was off target quite often. That's been less true so far this season, but he's had the good fortune of playing against a couple of friendly defenses. The Falcons' schedule does include a few games against high-quality defenses through the rest of the year (most notably the Vikings in Week 12), but it's not overly imposing. Penix might have a chance to keep this up, particularly if his accuracy improvement on intermediate and deep passes sticks. If that's just a two-week blip, though (which is certainly possible given the very small sample size and the level of competition), then some regression could be in store for this Atlanta offense.
